learning_outcomes.text: Understand how and why climate change necessitates a transformation towards sustainable mobility.
Distinguish the most important mobile drive systems according to their respective advantages, disadvantages, and areas of application.
Understand the basics of the function and construction of piston engines.
Understand the basics of the function and design of powertrains with fuel cells.
Understand the basics of the function and design of powertrains with battery-electric drives.
Understand the basics of the function and design of hybrid powertrains.
Describe which drive system is best suited for a specific application.
Interpret the influence of the energy carrier's role on the sustainability of the entire drive system.
Abstract the most important characteristics of modern drive systems.

syllabus_topics: Internal combustion engines and sustainable fuels
assessment_rules: The primary assessment is a 90-minute written examination. A simulation practical can be completed and presented by each student, leading to bonus points based on its qualitative elaboration and presentation. These bonus points are additionally credited to the examination performance, with a maximum of 10 percent bonus points possible relative to the points achievable in the examination. There is no claim to the implementation of this bonus system.
